messages:
maya.chen: quick heads-up — after the int4 quant run on q4b-multilang we see a ~4.2% jump in deid failures for short prompts (<32 tokens) in multiple scripts :eyes:
arjun.patel: ugh — I pulled a diff of token counts, looks like some tokens get split differently after quantized tokenmap recompute. histogram: https://s3.redwood-inference/test-artifacts/q4b-multilang/token-hist.png
sam.k: are we sure it's the tokenization and not the postprocess comparator? did we run NFKC normalisation before dedupe?
maya.chen: good q. i confirmed no extra norm step ran in the int4 pipeline — it's using raw tokenizer v2 mapping. older runs used nfkc normalize + fold.
priya.rao: can you paste a minimal repro example? i can try a local roundtrip.
arjun.patel: repro pair (short):
```
input: "تجربة"  # arabic word, 6 char
old tokens: [345, 678]
new tokens: [345, 12, 678]
```
counts change => dedupe sees different fingerprint.
sam.k: ok that split explains new dup/no-dup mismatch in the sampler. labeler pipeline compares fingerprint(token_ids) => rerouting.
maya.chen: proposal: 1) run a tokenmap-normalize pass to re-fingerprint the *candidate* set (not golden) with nfkc + fold then dedupe; 2) create a 200-sample micro-audit (multiscript) from the flagged differences for manual review; 3) hold golden_v3 freeze until audit done.
priya.rao: I can requeue the flagged set to labeling if you give me the s3 keys. prefer a targeted job: 2k samples, priority "ml-audit".
arjun.patel: s3 prefix created: s3://redwood-ci/q4b-multilang/int4-tokenmap-fails/ - contains csv of ids. run to re-fingerprint: `scripts/tools/refingerprint.py --norm nfkc --input csv --out s3://.../refingered.csv`
```bash
# quick refingerprint command
python3 scripts/tools/refingerprint.py \
  --norm nfkc --casefold \
  --tokenizer v2 --input s3://redwood-ci/q4b-multilang/fails.csv \
  --output s3://redwood-ci/q4b-multilang/refingered.csv
```
label-ops-bot: Created label job 5237 for owner priya.rao, 2000 samples, tag: multilang-tokenmap-audit. ETA: 48h. :white_check_mark:
priya.rao: acked. will assign to native-linguists first pass, then ML review.
sam.k: i'll run a quick eval comparing model outputs on the micro-audit with the previous fp32 baseline and attach diff logs to the job. script: `evals/compare_outputs.py --baseline s3://baselines/fp32/ --candidate s3://int4/q4b/ --ids s3://.../micro_ids.csv`
maya.chen: good. also note: metrics to watch = deid-false-positive rate, duplication-rate, and token-length-shift. if deid FP > 2% we rollback int4 for multilang.
arjun.patel: created canary set `canary/int4-tokenmap-spotcheck/200`. i'll post results here after the label job completes. :thumbsup:
maya.chen: thanks. action items: arjun -> run refingerprint and create micro-audit (done), priya -> label job owner, sam -> run baseline vs candidate diffs and surface any hallucination/regression cases. freeze golden_v3 until audit complete. ping me for blockers.
priya.rao: noted, will ping if labeling capacity conflicts with translations team.
arjun.patel: quick follow — should we add a pre-fingerprint normalization step to the int4 CI to avoid future drift? seems cheap.
sam.k: +1. small patch to pipeline: run nfkc + casefold before tokenize when model_lang != 'en'. low risk.
maya.chen: agree — add as canary opt-in for now, roll to default after audit.
label-ops-bot: Label job 5237 status: queued. ETA worker allocation ~2h.
maya.chen: perfect. thanks everyone :pray:
